card.title: Operations Director
card.description:
**Job Summary**

The Operations Director leads daily operations and strategic initiatives to strengthen performance across the business. You’ll guide teams, manage financial results, and turn operational data into clear priorities. This role works closely with executive leaders and customer-facing teams to improve processes, support business development, and deliver dependable customer service.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead operations management, business management, and strategic planning; align projects and resources with business priorities.
* Direct team management, executive-level team management, and team leadership; build capability through team development and clear managerial communication.
* Guide project management, process improvement, and lean management practices to improve workflows and operational outcomes.

**Skills**

* Leadership, management, supervising experience, operations management, operational management, and business management.
* Project management, strategic management, strategic planning, process improvement, and lean management.

Pay: $53,800.00 - $64,900.00 per year

Work Location: In person

card.title: Director of Operations
card.description:
**U C Coatings Director of Operations**

**Reports to** President

**Location** Based at a U-C Coatings facility; Buffalo, NY or Kenosha, WI preferred

**Travel** Approximately 25-35%, including regular travel to all four sites and 3PL partners

**Scope** Buffalo, Kenosha, Seattle and Portland manufacturing sites; 3PLs; supply chain and sourcing; customer service

**Position summary**

U-C Coatings manufactures specialty coatings, wood protection and repair products for industrial and consumer markets. The **Director of Operations** leads the people, processes and resources that turn customer demand into safe, reliable production and accurate, timely delivery.

Reporting to the President, this leader is accountable for operating performance across four sites and the supporting supply chain, sourcing, logistics and customer service functions. The role requires regular time on the production floor, strong financial judgment, and the ability to develop capable site and functional leaders in a lean organization.

**Manufacturing and site leadership**

* Lead site leaders in Buffalo, NY, Kenosha, WI, Seattle, WA, and Portland, OR; establish clear responsibilities, operating standards and performance expectations across the network.
* Translate demand into production, staffing and capacity plans; improve batch scheduling, filling, packaging, labor productivity and equipment utilization.
* Improve yield, reduce scrap and rework, and address recurring downtime through preventive maintenance, root cause analysis and practical process improvements.
* Evaluate production allocation, interplant transfers, capital investments and facility changes to improve service, cost and available capacity.

**Supply chain and sourcing**

* Own procurement and supplier performance for raw materials, packaging, purchased products and operating supplies; negotiate pricing, terms and service commitments.
* Lead monthly demand and supply planning with Sales and Finance; align forecasts, purchasing and production with service goals and working capital requirements.
* Set replenishment and inventory policies by item and site; improve inventory accuracy, reduce excess and obsolete stock, and prevent material shortages.
* Develop qualified alternate sources and continuity plans for critical inputs; coordinate supplier and material changes with Technical and Quality before implementation.

**Logistics and third party warehousing**

* Manage 3PL contracts, service standards and performance reviews, including inventory reconciliation, order accuracy, shipping performance, claims and invoice audits.
* Control inbound, outbound, parcel, LTL and interplant freight costs; improve packaging, carrier selection and routing while meeting customer requirements.

**Customer Service**

* Lead Customer Service from order receipt through fulfillment; improve order entry accuracy, acknowledgments, delivery commitments and response times.
* Connect Customer Service, Sales, planning, plants and 3PLs so customers receive reliable commitments and proactive updates on shortages or delays.
* Resolve escalated service issues, returns and credits with Sales, Finance and Technical; use complaint and shipping error trends to eliminate repeat failures.

**Safety quality and compliance**

* Hold site leaders accountable for safe operations, training, inspections, incident reporting and timely corrective action; maintain clear escalation and stop-work authority.
* Partner with internal specialists and outside advisers to meet applicable workplace safety, environmental, storage, waste and shipping requirements at each site.
* Ensure operating teams follow approved formulations, batch records, quality checks, labeling and lot traceability; support product launches and process changes with Technical and Quality.

**Financial management and people leadership**

* Own operating budgets and explain labor, material, freight and overhead variances with Finance; deliver verified savings and capital projects with clear returns.
* Coach and evaluate site and functional leaders; build staffing, cross-training and succession plans, and address performance issues promptly with HR support.
* Run weekly site and consolidated scorecard reviews covering service, cost, quality, inventory and people; assign owners and deadlines and verify corrective actions.

**Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including at least five years leading managers or major operating functions.
* Demonstrated success leading multiple manufacturing sites or a comparably complex manufacturing and distribution network; ability to lead dispersed teams.
* Practical experience with procurement, inventory planning, logistics, outsourced warehousing and customer fulfillment; strong cost and financial analysis skills.
* Experience with ERP and MRP systems, Excel, operating scorecards and continuous improvement; ability to turn data into decisions and sustained results.
* Bachelor's degree in operations, supply chain, engineering, business or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Coatings, chemicals, adhesives, sealants or other batch manufacturing experience is strongly preferred.

**Measures of success**

Accountable measures include safety controls; on-time, in-full delivery; labor efficiency; yield and cost of poor quality; inventory accuracy and turns; supplier and 3PL performance; freight costs; order accuracy; and leadership development. Agree on targets with the CEO after validating baselines.

**Initial priorities and working environment**

Within 90 days, assess the sites and key partners, validate scorecards, and agree on an improvement plan with owners, deadlines and financial impact. Work includes office, plant and warehouse activities, required PPE (company-provided), regular travel and occasional support outside business hours. Essential duties may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

**COMPANY DESCRIPTION:**

U-C Coatings is a leading manufacturer and supplier of premium wood protection products. For more than 50 years, our products have been used in a variety of industries, including hardwood and softwood logging and lumber production, wood products, manufacturing, woodworking, and wood decking markets.

Our products are used worldwide to protect, conserve, and enhance forest resources. Our goal is to help our customers achieve more with less waste and provide the highest level of protection for their products.

**ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:**

This role is an in-person role located within the company’s Kenosha, WI location. There is a moderate noise level within the work environment. Compliance with applicable Company policies including maintaining a drug-free workplace and adhering to all safety policies and procedures is required.

**DISCLAIMERS:**

UC Coatings, LLC reserves the right to revise, change or modify the duties and responsibilities of this position at any time to meet business needs. This job description may not list all duties for this position. This job description is not a contract of employment, and all UC Coatings, LLC employment unless otherwise disclosed is “at will” and either the incumbent or UC Coatings, LLC may terminate employment at any time for any reason.

UC Coatings, LLC is an Equal opportunity, inclusive employer and will consider all applicants for employment with the Company based on merit, competence, and qualifications without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local law.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

Experience:

* Operations management: 5 years (Required)

Willingness to travel:

* 50% (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

card.title: Director of Operations
card.description:
**Position Overview**

Maltz Jupiter Theatre (MJT) is Florida's only LORT B+ regional theatre, with a 659-seat mainstage, the 198-seat Island Theatre, the Goldner Conservatory, the Wardrobe gift shop, VIP lounges and a growing campus. The Director of Operations becomes the single point of accountability for the building and the patron experience, from an air-conditioning issue, leaks to a sold-out opening night.

The Director of Operations is responsible for the day-to-day running of the Maltz Jupiter Theatre campus so that every performance, class, event and donor experience happens in a safe, clean, fully working building. This is a senior leadership role, not a hands-on trades role. The Director of Operations plans, assigns, follows up and is accountable for results, while maintenance staff, cleaners, House Managers and vendors execute the work.

The Director of Operations is responsible for the management, maintenance, safety and operational excellence of the Theatre's facilities, and develops and executes a long-term facilities plan for asset replacement, sustainability and risk management. This position reports to the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive.

**Key Responsibilities**

The Director of Operations is accountable for every area below. The work itself is executed by staff, volunteers and vendors whom the Director of Operations directs and follows up with.

1. Facilities and Building Systems

* Oversee the condition and performance of the entire Theatre including, but not limited to, the MainStage, Island Theatre, Goldner Conservatory, offices, lobbies, Wardrobe gift shop, Green Room Club Level, GR2 and future spaces such as the Scene.

* Oversee HVAC performance and response, including air-conditioning leaks, humidity, temperature complaints, and chiller and air-handler issues. Ensure root causes are repaired, not just the symptoms.

* Oversee roofing, plumbing, electrical, elevators, fire suppression, generators, non-theatrical lighting, doors and hardware, parking lot, landscaping and signage.

* Monitor moisture control and mold prevention, especially during dark periods, and coordinate professional remediation when needed.

* Build and execute a preventive maintenance calendar for all major systems, with service records, warranties, permits and equipment manuals kept current.

* Hold an annual facility condition review and recommend a multi-year capital repair and replacement plan to the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive and the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Maintain an asset inventory and forecast timely replacement of furniture, fixtures, carpeting, HVAC, lighting and equipment.

* Oversee environmental sustainability and energy efficiency initiatives.

2. Work Orders and Project Follow-Through

* Own the JotForm maintenance request system: Review each submission and ensure every request is logged, prioritized, assigned, tracked and closed.

* Review open requests daily and set response standards by urgency (for example, same-day for safety issues and leaks, 72 hours for routine repairs).

* Assign work to in-house maintenance and cleaning staff or the appropriate vendor, and confirm completion before a request is closed.

* Report weekly to leadership on open, overdue and completed work, and flag recurring problems.

* Manage small capital and renovation projects from scope through punch list, coordinating with contractors, designers and the Town as needed.

3. Vendors and Contracts

* Manage all building and operations vendors including, but not limited to, HVAC, janitorial supplies, pest control, elevator, fire and life safety, security monitoring, landscaping, waste and recycling, linens, bar and beverage suppliers, and others.

* Solicit bids, validate that contractors are licensed and insured, recommend vendors and negotiate service terms, with contracts executed through the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Hold vendors to service levels, track certificates of insurance and contract renewal dates.

* Approve vendor invoices for accuracy before they are provided to the Finance department for processing.

4. Front of House and Patron Experience

* Review incident and house reports after every performance.

* Ensure lobbies, restrooms, seating areas and accessible routes are clean, stocked and show-ready before doors open.

* Oversee ADA accommodations and assistive listening equipment in addition to the Front of House and Bar Manager, and serve as the escalation point for patron complaints about the facility or service.

* Coordinate with box office, development and marketing on opening nights, galas, donor events, the season announcement and community programs, as needed.

* Collaborate with Production on load-ins, load-outs and technical needs from a facilities perspective, and on scheduling building use among departments.

5. Bars, Concessions and Signature Experiences

* Supervise the Front of House and Bar Manger to ensure bar operations across the building are staffed, inventory is properly stocked, inventory counts are performed, cash handling with the Finance department, and liquor licensing and responsible-service compliance is maintained.

* Supervise the Building Facilities Manager who is responsible for room set ups and tear-downs for every event.

* Ensure the Front of House and Bar Manager delivers the operational side of Signature Experiences including, but not limited to, GR2, the Green Room Club Level Lounge, the future Scene, onstage seating packages and themed pre-show events, so the experience matches what was sold.

* Be available to fill in for the Front of House and Bar Manager in the event of an absence.

6. Volunteer Program (Indirect Oversight)

* Provide operational leadership for the Theatre’s 420 volunteers, working through the Volunteer Coordinator, who continues to recruit and schedule them.

* Ensure volunteers in operational roles (ushers, greeters, hospitality, event support) are trained in house procedures, safety and emergency protocols.

* Make sure staffing levels by performance and event match patron needs, and resolve conflicts between volunteer, staff and patron needs.

* Champion volunteer recognition alongside the Volunteer Coordinator.

7. Security, Access and Loss Prevention

* Oversee security systems including, but not limited to, alarms, access control, keys and building lock-up procedures.

* Work with the IT Manager on building security including cameras, access management, and workspace readiness (keys, access cards, phones and equipment) for new employee offices and visiting artists.

* Manage security staffing or contracted security for performances, galas and high-profile events.

* Investigate missing items, damage and building incidents. Maintain incident reports and coordinate with police and insurance as needed.

* Maintain the key and access register, issuing and revoking access as staff change.

* Manage and maintain the building-wide paging and communication systems.

8. Emergencies and On-Call Duty

* Serve as the primary on-call contact for the building 24/7, on a rotation with designated backups for nights off and vacations.

* Respond to alarms, leaks, power outages, break-ins and other after-hours events, and decide when to call vendors, police or fire.

* Oversee the Theatre’s emergency action plan as it relates to evacuation, severe weather and hurricane preparation and recovery, medical emergencies, active threat, and show-stop procedures.

* Run regular drills and training for staff, house managers and volunteers, and maintain emergency contact lists, evacuation plans, and first aid and AED readiness.

* Ensure the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive remains informed of any incident affecting safety, performances, donors or the press.

9. Safety and Compliance

* Serve as the Theatre's primary safety officer, ensuring the building meets fire code, life safety, OSHA, ADA, health department and occupancy requirements. Serve as lead for inspections with the fire marshal and the Town.

* Maintain safety data sheets, inspection logs, fire extinguisher and alarm testing records, and elevator certificates.

* Work with the Production department so front-of-house and building safety align with stage and backstage safety.

* Manage relationships with local emergency and law enforcement agencies.

* Partner with the Finance department on insurance renewals, claims and risk reviews.

10. Budget and Reporting

* Build and manage the operations, facilities, front-of-house and bar budgets, including annual and multi-year capital budgets, with the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Track spending against budget and identify potential savings in utilities, supplies and service contracts.

* Provide monthly operations reports to leadership and, when asked, to Board committees.

11. Staff Leadership and Cross-Department Coordination

* Hire, train, schedule, supervise and evaluate operations staff.

* Write and maintain standard operating procedures for building opening and closing, show days, events, rentals and emergencies.

* Lead a weekly operations meeting with production, box office, development, marketing, the Goldner Conservatory and the Volunteer Coordinator to review the week's calendar and building needs.

* Coordinate building use for rentals, community partners, Goldner Conservatory classes and camps, so every space is booked, set and turned over correctly.

12. Campus Growth

* Represent operations in planning for campus expansion, including visiting artist housing on the land across the street and new amenity spaces.

* Advise on maintainability, staffing and operating costs of new spaces before they open, and lead their move into day-to-day operation.

**Reporting Structure**

The Director of Operatins supervises the people who keep the building running and coordinates, without supervising, the people whose work depends on it.

**Direct reports**

Building Facilities Manager, Front of House Manager, contracted security

**Indirect / dotted-line**

Volunteer Coordinator (for operational volunteer roles); about 420 volunteers through the Coordinator, House Manager, House Attendants

**Key partners**

Director of Finance and Administration; Production and Technical Direction; Box Office; Development; Marketing; Goldner Conservatory

**External**

Building and service vendors, contractors, Town of Jupiter, fire marshal, police, insurance carriers

**QualificationsRequired**

* 5-7+ years of progressive experience in facilities, venue or operations management, with at least 3 years supervising staff and vendors.

* Experience running a performing arts center, theatre, arena, museum, hotel or similar public venue with large audiences.

* Working knowledge of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, life safety and building automation systems, enough to judge vendor recommendations and costs.

* Proven record of running a work-order or ticketing system and closing work reliably.

* Experience with project management, capital planning, and building and managing operating budgets and vendor contracts.

* Strong leadership, written and verbal communication, and organizational skills, with staff, board members, donors, patrons, visiting artists and contractors.

* Calm, decisive judgment in emergencies; comfortable being the person everyone calls.

* Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on problem solving, to be self-directed, and to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel, and online forms such as JotForm.

* Valid driver's license; ability to pass a background check; able to respond to the Theatre within about 30 minutes when on call.

* Professional conduct at all times, representing the Theatre positively to artists, partner organizations, vendors, donors, volunteers, patrons and Board members.

**Preferred**

* Bachelor's degree in facilities management, business, hospitality or arts administration, or equivalent experience.

* Certifications such as Facility Management Professional (FMP), Certified Facility Manager (CFM), OSHA 30, CPR/AED and first aid, and crowd management training.

* Experience with safety management and emergency preparedness protocols.

* Background in facilities management software or CMMS systems, and in LEED or sustainable facility practices.

* Front-of-house or hospitality leadership, including liquor service compliance.

* Experience with hurricane preparation and recovery in Florida.

* Experience working with volunteers in a nonprofit setting.

* Familiarity with theatre operations, production schedules and event logistics.

**Working Conditions**

* Schedule follows the Theatre and may include evenings, weekends and holidays, with a regular presence at performances and major events.

* On call 24/7 on a published rotation, including during hurricanes and other emergencies.

* Walks the full campus daily, climbs stairs and ladders, enters mechanical rooms and roof areas, and lifts up to 40 pounds occasionally.

Pay: $85,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

card.title: Director of Operations
card.description:
**TBK One** began as an environmental consulting firm, helping businesses meet environmental standards through expert guidance, compliance support, and team education. As demand grew across industries such as oil drilling, refining, and concrete manufacturing, the company developed and manufactured its own eco-friendly industrial cleaning solutions to protect both equipment and the environment. Leveraging its expertise in environmental science, manufacturing, packaging, warehousing, and distribution, TBK One expanded its capabilities to support the broader operational needs of other businesses. Today, TBK One is a full-service partner for small and medium-sized businesses, delivering integrated, sustainable solutions backed by more than 20 years of environmental expertise.

**OUR VISION:** To be the premier provider of sustainable and innovative chemical solutions, transforming the way industries blend, package, and distribute their products.

**OUR MISSION:** To provide exceptional chemical blending and distribution services, ensuring quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction at every step.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Director of Operations is a senior leadership role responsible for day-to-day execution across blending, manufacturing, packaging, quality, warehousing, and distribution. Reporting directly to the CEO/Owner, this position serves as the primary point of operational accountability, translating company priorities into clear plans, scorecards, and measurable results while developing the operations team and organizational structure to support continued growth.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Operational Leadership & Strategy**

* Own end-to-end accountability for TBK One's daily operations, including blending, manufacturing, packaging, quality control, warehousing, and distribution.
* Translate enterprise and department-level priorities into clear operational plans, scorecards, and accountability for the operations team.
* Build and evolve the operations team structure to support growth and ensure the right people are in the right seats.
* Serve as the senior operational decisionmaker for production scheduling, capacity planning, and resource allocation.
* Report to the CEO/Owner on operational performance, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.

**Manufacturing, Production & Capacity**

* Oversee custom chemical blending, product formulation, reformulation, and full-service manufacturing operations.
* Partner with operational staff to measure plant capacity, throughput, and efficiency and close performance gaps as volume grows.
* Coordinate with Sales to establish realistic production expectations and timelines based on client needs, capacity, and operational requirements.
* Ensure equipment, staffing, and scheduling are aligned to meet customer commitments and seasonal demand.
* Provide operational input on pricing strategies, lead times, and cost estimates for custom blending and packaging products, as needed.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives to reduce waste, downtime, and production costs without compromising quality.

**Quality, Compliance & Safety**

* Maintain rigorous quality control standards across raw material inspection, in-process testing, and finished goods.
* Partner with the EHS (Environmental, Health and Safety) Advisor and Accounting/Finance leadership on environmental and regulatory requirements affecting operations, including chemical storage and EPA reporting.
* Champion SOP adherence and documentation across operational areas to support consistent process execution.
* Build and reinforce a strong safety-first culture throughout the warehouse and production floor.

**Warehousing, Distribution & Inventory**

* Oversee warehousing operations, inventory accuracy, and outbound distribution to support on-time, complete fulfillment.
* Optimize logistics and distribution workflows, leveraging TBK One's DFW location and highway access.
* Implement and monitor systems for real-time inventory visibility, cycle counts, and demand forecasting to minimize production interruptions.

**People Leadership & Organizational Systems**

* Lead, manage, and develop operations personnel and managers, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and development priorities as the organization grows.
* Run effective team meetings within the EOS framework, including Level 10 meetings, and maintain department-level scorecards and accountabilities.
* Support hiring, onboarding, performance management, training, and development for operations roles.
* Partner with the CEO/Owner on organizational design and succession planning as the operations function scales.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in operations management, engineering, chemistry, supply chain, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 7+ years of progressive operations leadership experience, ideally in chemical manufacturing, industrial blending, or process manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing manufacturing, warehousing, and distribution functions simultaneously.
* Working knowledge of chemical safety, EPA/OSHA compliance, and quality control practices; DOT experience is a plus.
* Proven ability to build, manage, and develop teams, including managers or supervisors.
* Ability to operate with significant autonomy while maintaining strong alignment and communication with ownership/CEO.
* Experience with EOS or a similar operating system, including Rocks, scorecards, and Level 10 meetings, is strongly preferred.
* Knowledge of production and inventory planning systems is a plus.
* Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and leadership skills.

**Work Environment & Physical Requirements**

This position works in both an office setting and production/warehouse environments, with frequent presence required in manufacturing and warehousing areas. Exposure to industrial chemicals, equipment, and noise is expected. Appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) will be provided and must be worn in accordance with applicable safety protocols. The position requires the ability to walk, stand, and move throughout warehouse and production environments for extended periods.

Join us as we lead the way in environmental innovation! This role offers an exciting chance to influence industry standards while working in a vibrant environment that values leadership, collaboration, and forward-thinking solutions.

Pay: $120,000.00 - $130,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

card.title: Director of Broadcast Operations and Programming Services
card.description:
**SCOPE OF POSITION**

The Director of Broadcast Operations and Programming Services serves as the senior official responsible for oversight of the integrated day to-day broadcast and media distribution operations of WPSU; provides vision, strategic development and oversight of all content distribution across four broadcast television channels, three FM channels, works collaboratively in support of streaming and digital services; and serves as a member of the executive leadership team, providing strategic vision, key performance metrics, strategies and operational guidelines for the organization.

**MAJOR DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**STRATEGIC LEADERSHIP**

* Serve as a member of the executive leadership team, providing strategic vision, key performance metrics, strategies and operational guidelines for the organization.

* Represent the organization's interests by regularly engaging in communications and negotiations with the Public Broadcasting Service, National Public Radio, the Federal Communications Commission and other organizations as necessary, and ensure compliance with the policies of those organizations.

* Regularly engage with key stakeholders including viewer/listeners, donors, advisory board members, businesses, and the community at large to build collaborative relationships and to cultivate awareness and support of the organization.

**OPERATIONAL OVERSIGHT**

* Oversee and manage the integrated day-to-day broadcast and media distribution operations of WPSU, ensuring compliance with federal and state laws and regulations, broadcast industry standards, WPSU policies, and safety guidelines.

* Oversee and manage program development and production, broadcast engineering and operations, regulatory compliance, and reporting.

* Ensure that the stations project an on-air image of high production values and quality of content and that all technical standards are regularly measured and met.

* Lead or assist in station development functions. Work to cultivate donor support for new projects and ongoing services. Conceive entrepreneurial projects to generate revenue. Identify funding sources and develop funding proposals.

**PROGRAMMING AND DISTRIBUTION**

* Responsible for the vision, strategic development and oversight of all content distribution across our four broadcast television channels, three FM channels and our digital services in order to drive audience growth, diversification, engagement, retention, and financial support.

* Implement a cross-platform strategy to acquire, produce and distribute diverse programming content that attracts, maintains, and increases audience, consistent with the organization’s mission and themes, and addresses issues of particular local relevance to the diverse communities we serve.

* Negotiate contracts for the acquisition and distribution of program content, manage and ensure compliance with all applicable terms, rights and releases.

* Respond to viewer and listener inquiries about programming.

**SUPERVISION**

* Provide direct supervision to the TV and FM broadcast operations, traffic, and programming staff, and the News Director.

* Ensure that applicable Human Resources and WPSU policies and procedures are followed. Work to identify and resolve related issues.

* Create and/or identify development opportunities for staff and training to enhance skills, leadership and foster growth.

* Lead and/or participate in interviewing and selection of new employees, work with supervisors, managers, and directors to set performance standards for staff and perform regular and ongoing review and evaluation.

* Foster and promote a team environment that celebrates and promotes a culture of diversity, safety and environmental consciousness.

**PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT**

* Remain competent and current in a rapidly evolving industry through self-directed professional reading, developing professional contacts with colleagues, attending professional development courses, presenting at conferences and engaging in other training and personal development opportunities.

**FINANCIAL**

* Oversee, develop and administer annual operating budgets that support our broadcast operations and administration, program acquisition, membership affiliation and more.

* Lead and/or participate in the planning and coordination of on-air fundraising campaigns as well as general WPSU fundraising efforts.

**Education:** Requires the knowledge obtained by receiving a Bachelor’s degree in a related discipline.

**Experience:** Proven leadership skills with a minimum of 4 years of experience directly supervising and managing staff. 5 or more years of full-time programming experience with knowledge of public media programs, audiences, editorial standards, and familiarity with ratings data.

**Technical Skills:** Must be technologically savvy, with fluent use of business software systems including Microsoft Office, (Word, Excel), and the ability to use content management systems and software tools. Experience with and capable of operating digital broadcast equipment required.
